answers.answer: Keep 4 gems per color and 5 gold. Reveal 3 nobles and permanently remove the other 7.
answers.evidence: Setup token table; removed nobles are out of the game permanently.

answers.answer: Three players: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four players: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count table.

answers.answer: Shuffle each development level separately. Put decks in a column, level 1 bottom, level 2 middle, level 3 top. Reveal 4 cards per level, 12 total. Youngest starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3; First Player.

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different colors; take 2 non-gold gems of one color if at least 4 are in that supply before taking; reserve 1 development if holding fewer than 3 reserved cards and take 1 gold if available; or purchase 1 face-up development or 1 card reserved on a previous turn, paying its cost after bonuses with gold usable as wild. You cannot take gems then buy, or reserve then buy the same card, in one turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: must perform exactly one of the following four actions; card you reserved on a previous turn.

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times.

answers.answer: You may take 2 green, leaving 2, because green starts at 4. You may not take 2 red from 3. Check the threshold before taking. Neither gem-taking action can take gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them; no gold.

answers.answer: Yes, temporarily holding 12 is allowed. Return 2 to end at 10; these may be newly drawn tokens. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: may temporarily exceed 10; return some or all ... just took; including gold.

answers.answer: Take 1 gold with the reservation, temporarily reaching 11, then return 1 token of your choice, possibly that gold, to end with 10. If gold is empty, reserve without gold and stay at 10.
answers.evidence: Reserve: no gold ... may still reserve; Token Hand Limit allows temporary excess and return of gold obtained by reserving.

answers.answer: Reserve 1 face-up market card or the top card of any one level deck. The deck card is not shown to opponents. Only its reserving player may buy a reserved card.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: face-up ... or ... top card ... without revealing; Reserved cards may only be purchased by the player who reserved them.

answers.answer: No reservation is allowed with 3 already reserved, even just to obtain gold. You cannot discard or exchange a reserved card to make room; only purchasing removes it from your hand.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another; only way to remove ... purchase it.

answers.answer: Immediately replace the level-2 card from the top of the level-2 deck. Face-up purchases use the same immediate refill from the corresponding level deck. Buying a reserved card creates no market gap, so needs no refill. If the corresponding deck is empty, a vacated market space stays empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: face-up card ... acquired ... or reserved ... immediately replaced ... same level; if deck empty ... remains empty.

answers.answer: Spend 1 green token, or 1 gold substituting for green; the 2 blue bonuses cover blue. If bonuses cover every color, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: example ... only need to spend 1 green token; gold substitutes; bonuses permanent; without spending any tokens.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses leave 1 blue, 1 black and 1 white to pay. Spend the blue for blue and the 2 gold for black and white. All 3 spent tokens return to supply. Your bonus cards remain with you permanently.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce costs; gold substitutes for any single gem; spent tokens returned to supply; permanent bonuses.

answers.answer: Buy 1 face-up development or 1 previously reserved development from your hand. Put purchased cards face up before you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so bonuses and prestige values stay visible to everyone at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase a Development Card; Place purchased development cards face-up ... sorted ... staggered ... visible ... at all times.

answers.answer: No: a white or gold token does not replace the missing white bonus. A third white bonus qualifies you at the end of your turn. Bonuses above the required quantities do not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: at least ... bonuses ... not gem tokens.

answers.answer: Choose exactly 1 noble. You cannot take both or refuse all visits. It uses no action and gives 3 prestige. Check eligibility at the end of your turn after your action.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: automatic; cannot refuse; not an action; choose one; at most one; 3 prestige points.

answers.answer: Place the noble face up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you.

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns. A takes no extra turn because the round then has equal turn counts. B is not guaranteed to win; another player may surpass B before the round ends.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: current round ... same number of turns; player who triggers ... may not necessarily win.

answers.answer: You reach 16. That triggers the end condition, which is 15 or more. Determine the winner after completing the current round, using final prestige totals.
answers.evidence: Noble tiles: 3 each; End-Game Trigger: 15 or more; winner at end of final round.

answers.answer: B wins: A and B tie at the highest prestige, 16, and B has fewer purchased developments, 9 versus 10. C's 15 loses despite fewer cards. Noble points count. B's 3 unpurchased reserved cards do not count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Winner: most prestige; Noble tile points count; tie: fewest development cards purchased.

answers.answer: No. Unpurchased reserved cards supply no prestige for score or trigger and no bonuses for purchases or nobles. These benefits come from purchased cards.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources: each purchased card; Payment: previously purchased development cards; Noble Visits: bonuses from purchased development cards.

answers.answer: No physical blue token is generated. The zero-prestige card gives a permanent blue bonus for future purchases and noble eligibility.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: each purchased development ... one bonus ... permanently; never generate tokens. Nobles require bonuses; prestige may be 0.

answers.answer: The blue card cannot discount its own purchase; only previously purchased cards reduce the cost, so you cannot buy it with those holdings. A newly purchased white bonus does count for the noble check at the end of this same turn.
answers.evidence: Payment: bonuses from previously purchased development cards; Noble Visits: end of their turn ... bonuses from purchased development cards.

answers.answer: Excess blue cannot pay green or generate tokens as change. Blue is covered; you still owe 2 green, payable with 2 green tokens or gold substitutions.
answers.evidence: Bonus Stacking: excess provides no benefit; no change; never generate tokens. Payment: bonuses of that color; gold substitutes.

answers.answer: Bonuses are permanent and not consumed by the first noble. If the second stays available, taking gems on your next turn can lead to receiving it at that turn's end. You cannot collect it on an opponent's intervening turn.
answers.evidence: Bonuses permanently; Noble Visits: at end of their turn; other nobles remain available for future turns.

answers.answer: Yes, you may reserve that face-up level-3 card while holding fewer than 3 reserved cards, without paying its printed purchase cost. Take 1 gold if available.
answers.evidence: Reserve: Take one development card ... face-up; Upon reserving ... take 1 gold. Cost payment is part of Purchase.

answers.answer: The blind reservation takes 1 top level-2 deck card into your hand. It neither removes nor refills a market card; 12 market cards remain. You cannot take a second card as a hand replacement.
answers.evidence: Reserve 1 development card; top card from any one ... decks; replacement applies when face-up grid card removed.

answers.answer: The 4 face-up cards remain available to buy or reserve. Buying one leaves its space empty permanently; the other 3 stay available.
answers.evidence: Purchase or reserve face-up cards; Card Replacement: if corresponding deck empty ... empty space ... remains empty.

answers.answer: Exhaustion does not end the game. The player may buy 1 affordable own previously reserved card, or take 1 non-gold gem from each of 3 different available colors, as their single action. Continue to the prestige end condition.
answers.evidence: Exhausting ... decks or ... market does not end the game; remaining legal actions, including purchasing reserved cards; Take 3 different colors.

answers.answer: Yes. Take the 3 different gems, temporarily reaching 13, and return all 3 newly taken tokens to finish with the same 10. No net gain is required.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: may temporarily exceed 10; may return some or all ... tokens they just took.

answers.answer: A's 2 spent gold return to supply. B takes 1 when reserving, leaving 1 gold in supply before any token-limit returns.
answers.evidence: Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply; reserving ... take 1 gold token.

answers.answer: Yes. You may purchase 1 affordable face-up level-3 card without first buying lower levels. The purchase rule has no level-unlocking prerequisite.
answers.evidence: Purchase a face-up development card from the grid ... by paying the gem token cost shown on the card.

answers.answer: You cannot skip the automatic noble. The development brings you to 15 and the noble adds 3, making 18. Players still due turns in the current round continue until all turn counts are equal.
answers.evidence: Noble visits automatic ... cannot refuse ... 3 points; current round completed ... same number of turns.

answers.answer: The game is over after D completes that turn. A does not start another round and nobody gets an extra turn: everyone has already had the same number of turns.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: current round is completed so ... same number of turns.

answers.answer: No new noble is revealed; removed nobles are permanently out of the game. The acquired tile goes face up in front of its recipient, leaving 2 nobles available in the middle.
answers.evidence: Removed during setup ... out of the game permanently; Place received noble face-up in front of you.

answers.answer: Emerald: green; diamond: white; sapphire: blue; onyx: black; ruby: red; gold joker: yellow. There are 90 development cards: 40 level 1, 30 level 2, 20 level 3.
answers.evidence: Components token color table and development card table.

answers.answer: You may pay 1 gold and keep the green. Gold can substitute for any single gem token; the spent gold returns to supply.
answers.evidence: Gold tokens ... can substitute for any single gem token. Spent gold tokens ... returned to the supply.

answers.answer: Yes: take 1 red, 1 blue, 1 green. The four-token minimum only applies to taking 2 of one color. The piles then have 0 red, 1 blue and 2 green.
answers.evidence: Take 3: 1 gem token from each of 3 different color piles; Take 2 requires at least 4.

answers.answer: A direct gold-for-red exchange is not a listed action or an authorized joker use. When purchasing, gold substitutes for any single gem token and spent gold returns to supply.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists exactly four actions; Gold Token Specifics: substitute for any gem color when purchasing a card.

answers.answer: You must choose exactly 1 of the four actions. Voluntarily passing while legal actions exist is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: a player must perform exactly one of the following four actions.

answers.answer: Sort the supply by color into 6 distinct gem and gold piles, within reach of all players.
answers.evidence: Setup step 5: 6 distinct piles sorted by color, within reach of all players.

answers.answer: Your final prestige is 15: 12 from purchased cards plus 3 from the noble. Unspent gold and other gems add no points.
answers.evidence: Prestige Point Sources lists purchased developments and nobles, 3 each.

answers.answer: Shuffle the noble tiles before revealing the required number. Hand-picking preferred nobles instead would not follow that setup instruction.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4: Shuffle the noble tiles. Reveal a number ... players plus one.
